source_meta._title: io.netty.handler.codec.EncoderException when evaluating too many entity selectors in chat preview

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition using an unmodified vanilla dedicated server and a client both running exactly 1.19 Pre-release 1. A local server on the same computer is the simplest deterministic arrangement, using localhost as the address. Use a newly generated normal/default world with no plugins, proxy, custom server implementation, or datapacks. Java 17 is required for this Minecraft version. The report does not specify a world seed, game mode, difficulty, or minimum entity count.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher can run the historical Java Edition version 1.19 Pre-release 1; snapshots/pre-releases are enabled in the launcher's Installations screen.
The vanilla dedicated-server JAR for exactly 1.19 Pre-release 1 is available in a separate test directory and is not a 1.19 Pre-release 2 or later server.
Java 17 is installed and available through the command line.
The server EULA can be accepted before starting the test server.
The client and server use the same affected version, 1.19 Pre-release 1.
Chat preview is enabled in server.properties with the exact property previews-chat=true.
The test player is granted operator permissions so that the client accepts and previews the /say command.
The client-side Chat Preview option is enabled.
Only one trigger attempt is necessary; do not repeatedly reconnect and reproduce the exception after the observation subsystem has captured it.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, open Installations, enable the option that shows snapshots if necessary, and create or select an installation whose version is exactly 1.19 Pre-release 1. Do not select the fixed version 1.19 Pre-release 2.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation explicitly displays 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: Create an empty directory for the dedicated test server. Place the vanilla 1.19 Pre-release 1 server JAR in this directory and, for the commands below, name it server.jar. Open a terminal or command prompt with this directory as its working directory.
steps.success_cue: The working directory contains the affected-version server JAR named server.jar.

steps.action: Run the server once to generate its configuration files. Enter the command in the terminal from the server directory. This first launch should stop because the EULA has not yet been accepted.
steps.success_cue: The server directory now contains eula.txt and server.properties, and the server process has stopped or reports that the EULA must be accepted.

steps.action: Open eula.txt in a plain-text editor. After reviewing and accepting the Minecraft EULA, replace eula=false with eula=true, then save the file without changing its filename.
steps.success_cue: The saved eula.txt contains the line eula=true.

steps.action: While the server is stopped, open server.properties in a plain-text editor. Find the previews-chat property and set it to true. If the generated file does not already contain the property, add it as its own line. Save the file.
steps.success_cue: The saved server.properties contains exactly one active previews-chat=true line.

steps.action: Start the dedicated server again from its directory using the Java command. Leave this terminal open because it is also the server console.
steps.success_cue: The console reports that server startup is complete, normally with a line containing Done, and remains ready to accept console input.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the launcher installation selected in step 1. At the title screen, verify that the displayed version is 1.19 Pre-release 1.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running client as 1.19 Pre-release 1.

steps.action: Before joining the server, open Options, then Chat Settings. Locate Chat Preview and toggle it to ON. Return to the title screen after confirming the setting.
steps.exact_input: Options -> Chat Settings -> Chat Preview: ON
steps.success_cue: Chat Preview is displayed as ON in Chat Settings.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Multiplayer and use Direct Connection or Add Server. For a server running on the same computer, enter localhost as the server address and join it. If the server is on another computer, enter that server's reachable address instead.
steps.success_cue: The player has joined the dedicated server, surrounding terrain has rendered, and normal player movement responds without initial chunk-loading delay.

steps.action: In the dedicated-server console, grant the connected test player operator permissions so /say is available to that player. Replace <playername> with the exact in-game player name. Because this is entered in the server console, do not include a leading slash.
steps.success_cue: The server console confirms that the named player was made a server operator, and the player remains connected.

steps.action: Leave the player in the normally generated world. Do not clear entities, switch to a void world, install plugins, or otherwise reduce the ordinary loaded entity population. Wait until nearby chunks are rendered and movement is responsive before opening chat.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a normally generated, fully loaded area of the server world with no loading pause in progress.

steps.action: Press the Open Chat control, which is T by default. Begin the command by typing /say followed by one entity selector. Do not press Enter; the command must remain in the chat edit box so chat preview evaluates it while it is being typed.
steps.success_cue: The chat screen remains open, /say @e is visible in the edit box, and the command has not been submitted.

steps.action: Pause briefly until the chat preview has had an opportunity to update for the current text. Continue only when the client UI is responsive; do not press Enter at any point.
steps.success_cue: The chat screen is still active and ready for another token to be typed after the current preview request.

steps.action: Append a space followed by another @e selector to the existing command. Add selectors one at a time rather than submitting the command. After each complete token, briefly allow chat preview to process it, then append another identical token. First build toward the report's concrete ten-selector example; if the observation subsystem has not yet signaled completion, continue adding one space-plus-@e token at a time. Do not press Enter. The individual append that causes the oversized preview response is the trigger action.
steps.success_cue: Immediately after each append, the unsent command contains one additional complete @e token and a new chat-preview evaluation has been initiated.

stor.handoff_condition: During step 14, hand control to the observation subsystem immediately after each additional complete " @e" token is appended while the chat screen remains in command-editing mode. The command must still be unsent, Chat Preview must remain enabled, and Enter must not be pressed. The observation subsystem should monitor the client connection state and dedicated-server console while selector tokens are added, and should stop further input after capturing the first trigger occurrence.
uncertainties: The report does not state an exact selector count that always reaches the oversized-preview threshold. It gives ten selectors as a concrete example but says to continue typing @e until the trigger occurs; the necessary count can vary with the number and representation of entities currently loaded.

The report describes a normal world but provides no seed, coordinates, game mode, difficulty, or required entity population. The plan therefore uses a fresh default server world and does not artificially add or remove entities.

The report says to create a server but does not explicitly distinguish vanilla dedicated server software from other server implementations. A vanilla dedicated server is selected because the supplied stack trace identifies the affected vanilla server JAR and this avoids plugin or proxy interference.

Operator status is not explicitly listed in the report. It is added as a practical execution requirement so the player can type a valid /say command and receive its chat preview rather than being blocked by command permissions.
Typing selectors sequentially is preserved from the report. Pasting a fully constructed command may issue a different number or timing of preview requests and is therefore not used.
The fixed version 1.19 Pre-release 2 must not be used for reproduction, even though it appears in the report as a fix version.

source_meta._title: Uploading a world to a snapshot Realm wipes it

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition client running exactly 26.1 Snapshot 9, first in singleplayer and then through a Mojang-hosted Snapshot Realm associated with the same authenticated account. The account must own or otherwise have configuration access to the Snapshot Realm; ordinary invited-member access is insufficient for uploading a world. Use a disposable Realm world slot over a stable internet connection.
preconditions: Install and launch exactly 26.1 Snapshot 9, not 26.1 Pre-Release 2 or any newer version.
Sign in through the Minecraft Launcher with the Microsoft account that owns or can configure the Snapshot Realm.
Ensure the Snapshot Realm is active and accessible from 26.1 Snapshot 9.
Reserve a disposable Realm world slot. If that slot contains anything important, download or otherwise back it up before beginning because uploading replaces the slot's current world.
Use a newly created, disposable singleplayer world for this reproduction. Do not use an important existing world.
Use an unmodified client without third-party mods. No custom resource pack, data pack, seed, or experiment is required by the report.
Keep the newly created world small so that its upload can complete without unrelated world-size or network complications.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, go to the Installations tab, enable the option that makes snapshot versions available if it is disabled, and create or select an installation whose version is exactly 26.1 Snapshot 9.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation explicitly lists 26.1 Snapshot 9 as its game version.

steps.action: Start that installation and wait for the Minecraft: Java Edition main menu to finish loading. Check the version text displayed on the menu before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and its version text identifies the running client as 26.1 Snapshot 9.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to begin making the local world that will later be uploaded.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the world name to a unique, easily identifiable value and select Creative as the game mode. Leave the seed unspecified and leave experiments and data packs at their defaults.
steps.success_cue: The configured world is named "MC-306502 local source" and Creative mode is selected.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the newly generated singleplayer world.

steps.action: Do not modify the world immediately. Wait until nearby terrain is rendered and ordinary movement responds without initial chunk-loading pauses.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is visible, the player can move normally, and the initial loading overlay is gone.

steps.action: Press E, or the rebound Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to find a Block of Gold and move a stack into any hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots at the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A stack of Blocks of Gold is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E or Esc, select the hotbar slot containing the Blocks of Gold, and use the Place/Use Item control, right-click by default, to construct a vertical pillar three gold blocks tall immediately beside the player's initial area. Place the first block on the ground, then place the next two on top of it.
steps.success_cue: A conspicuous three-block-tall gold pillar is standing near the local world's starting location.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory again. Search for Chest and Diamond, then move both items to separate hotbar slots.
steps.success_cue: A Chest and a stack of Diamonds are both available in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory, select the Chest, and right-click an empty ground block directly beside the gold pillar to place the chest.
steps.success_cue: A chest is placed adjacent to the gold pillar.

steps.action: Right-click the placed chest to open its container interface. Move the Diamond stack from the player inventory into a chest slot, then close the chest interface with E or Esc.
steps.success_cue: The chest has been closed after a Diamond stack was placed inside it.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory once more, obtain another Diamond stack, and leave it in one of the player's hotbar slots. Close the inventory without putting this second stack in the chest.
steps.success_cue: The world contains the gold pillar and diamond-filled chest, while a separate Diamond stack remains in the player's hotbar as a player-data marker.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay and record or capture the player's displayed X, Y, and Z coordinates while standing beside the pillar and chest. Press F3 again to close the overlay. If the keyboard assigns media functions to the F-keys, use Fn+F3.
steps.success_cue: The coordinates of the pillar-and-chest test location have been retained for later comparison and the debug overlay is closed.

steps.action: Press Esc and select Save and Quit to Title. Wait until the main menu has fully returned before taking another action.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and the singleplayer session has closed normally.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, select "MC-306502 local source", and select Play Selected World. Wait until its terrain finishes loading and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player has re-entered the saved local source world and can move normally.

steps.action: At the recorded location, confirm only that the source save is prepared correctly: the three-block gold pillar and adjacent chest are present, the chest still contains the Diamond stack when opened, and the separate Diamond stack remains in the player's hotbar. Close the chest after this setup check.
steps.success_cue: The local source save demonstrably contains persisted block, container, and player-inventory progress before upload.

steps.action: Press Esc, select Save and Quit to Title again, and wait for the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The source world has been saved and the Minecraft main menu is displayed.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Minecraft Realms and wait for the owned and invited Realms list to load from the service.
steps.success_cue: The Realms screen is responsive and the account's Snapshot Realm is visible.

steps.action: Select the Snapshot Realm owned by the logged-in account, then select Configure. Do not select an ordinary invited Realm for which the account lacks configuration rights.
steps.success_cue: The configuration interface for the intended Snapshot Realm is open.

steps.action: Open the Realm's world-management screen and select the disposable world slot intended for the test. Use the Edit World control for that slot if the interface requires it.
steps.success_cue: The disposable slot's management screen is open and presents the control for uploading or replacing its world.

steps.action: Select Upload World. If this build labels the equivalent world-replacement control as Replace World, use that control instead. Wait for the list of locally saved singleplayer worlds to appear.
steps.success_cue: A selection screen containing local singleplayer saves is visible.

steps.action: Select the local world named "MC-306502 local source" and activate the final confirmation control that starts uploading it to the selected Snapshot Realm slot. Accept the warning that the slot's existing world will be replaced.
steps.success_cue: The upload has started and an upload progress screen or progress indicator is visible.

steps.action: Wait without canceling, closing Minecraft, changing installations, or interrupting the network connection. Continue only when the interface reports that the upload/replacement has completed and returns control through a Done, Let's Go, or equivalent completion control.
steps.success_cue: The upload process has completed without an error message and the Realm slot is available for play.

steps.action: Return to the Realm's main screen if necessary, select the same Snapshot Realm and uploaded slot, and select Play. If the successful-upload screen offers to enter the Realm directly, use that option instead.
steps.success_cue: The client begins connecting to the selected Snapshot Realm rather than reopening the local singleplayer world.

steps.action: Wait until the Realm connection and dimension loading finish. Do not begin evaluating transferred blocks, chest contents, or player data until surrounding chunks have rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside the uploaded Snapshot Realm world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement is responsive.

stor.handoff_condition: The upload of "MC-306502 local source" to the disposable Snapshot Realm slot has completed, and the player has subsequently entered that Realm world with nearby chunks fully rendered and movement responsive. Hand off now so the observation subsystem can compare the loaded Realm state with the recorded local source state.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode, seed, coordinates, or exact pre-upload progress. This plan uses a new Creative-mode world, a gold pillar, a diamond-filled chest, and a Diamond stack in the player hotbar as deterministic practical markers; Creative mode is not asserted as a requirement of the bug.
The report says the problem was reproduced both with old worlds and with worlds newly created in the current snapshot. This plan chooses the simpler new-world-in-26.1-Snapshot-9 variant.

The report does not provide the exact 26.1 Snapshot 9 Realms button layout. The standard Java Realms path uses Realm configuration, world management/Edit World, and Upload World; some interface revisions may label the equivalent replacement action Replace World.
The report does not explicitly state the Realm subscription, ownership, or permission setup, but uploading a local world operationally requires access to the Realm's configuration controls.
The report mentions media attachments, but their contents were not supplied. The plan therefore relies only on the written description and comments.

No exact seed is supplied. The seed must remain whatever the newly created source world generates; the executor must not recreate a second local world from that seed as a substitute for uploading the prepared save.

source_meta._title: Player object text components in server status messages (MotD) are no longer replaced by fallback text

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Pre-Release 2 client and a Python 3 mock Minecraft status server running on the same computer. The mock server listens on TCP port 25565 and is accessed through the loopback address 127.0.0.1. A vanilla or dedicated Minecraft server is not required, and the client must not join the mock server; the reproduction occurs in the Multiplayer server list.
preconditions: Minecraft Java Edition 26.1 Pre-Release 2 is installed and selectable in the Minecraft Launcher.
Python 3 is installed, and the `python` command invokes it from Command Prompt or PowerShell.
TCP port 25565 is available; stop any Minecraft server or other program already using that port before starting the mock server.
The Minecraft client and Python script will run on the same computer so that the exact address 127.0.0.1 reaches the mock server.
The executor can create and save a plain-text `.py` file.
If the operating system displays a firewall prompt for Python, permit the local connection needed for the test.
Keep the terminal running after starting the script. Closing it stops the mock server.

steps.action: Open Command Prompt or PowerShell and verify that the Python command is available.
steps.success_cue: The terminal prints a Python 3 version instead of reporting that `python` is unknown or unavailable.

steps.action: Open a plain-text editor and create a new file named `mc306860_mock_status.py`. Ensure the file is saved with the `.py` extension rather than `.py.txt`.
steps.success_cue: A writable plain-text file named `mc306860_mock_status.py` exists.

steps.action: Paste the report's mock status-server script into `mc306860_mock_status.py` exactly as supplied, then save the file.
steps.success_cue: The file is saved, begins with `import socket`, and ends with the call to `main()`.

steps.action: Open Command Prompt or PowerShell in the directory containing `mc306860_mock_status.py`. One way to do this on Windows is to open that folder in File Explorer, click the address bar, type `powershell`, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The terminal's current directory is the folder containing `mc306860_mock_status.py`.

steps.action: Start the mock status server by executing the saved Python file. Do not close this terminal after the command starts.
steps.success_cue: The terminal displays `Mock server running on port 25565. Add 127.0.0.1 in Minecraft.` followed by `Press Ctrl+C to stop.` and does not return to the command prompt.

steps.action: If the operating system displays a firewall prompt for Python, allow the connection. Leave the mock-server terminal open and running in the background.
steps.success_cue: The Python process remains active without a traceback or an error stating that port 25565 could not be bound.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Minecraft Java Edition `26.1 Pre-Release 2`, and launch it. Do not substitute the fixed version `26.1 Pre-Release 3`.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is open and identifies the running version as 26.1 Pre-Release 2.

steps.action: From the Minecraft main menu, click `Multiplayer`. If a standard pre-release or multiplayer warning screen appears, acknowledge it to continue to the Multiplayer server list.
steps.success_cue: The Multiplayer server-list screen is visible.

steps.action: Click `Add Server` at the bottom of the Multiplayer screen.
steps.success_cue: The Edit Server Info screen is open and contains fields for `Server Name` and `Server Address`.

steps.action: In the `Server Name` field, enter a recognizable label for the mock server. This label is only for identifying the entry and is not part of the network payload.
steps.success_cue: The Server Name field contains `MC-306860 Mock Server`.

steps.action: Click the `Server Address` field, remove any existing contents, and enter the loopback address exactly as supplied in the report. Do not add `http://`, a path, or spaces. Because the script uses the default Minecraft port 25565, no explicit port suffix is required.
steps.success_cue: The Server Address field contains exactly `127.0.0.1`.

steps.action: Click `Done` once to save the server entry and return to the Multiplayer server list. This causes the client to request status information from the Python mock server.
steps.success_cue: The Multiplayer list is visible and contains the saved entry named `MC-306860 Mock Server`.

steps.action: Do not double-click the server or press `Join Server`. Wait for the server-list status request to complete. Use the terminal as the readiness signal: wait until it prints a client connection line and a `Payload sent:` line for the status JSON.
steps.success_cue: The Python terminal has printed `[+] Client connected from ...`, followed by `Payload sent: ...`, and the saved server entry has finished its status poll in the Multiplayer list.

steps.action: Keep the Multiplayer list open with the completed mock-server entry visible. Do not refresh the list, join the server, stop the Python process, or navigate away before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The mock server's status description has just been received and rendered beneath the saved server name, and the entry remains visible for inspection.

stor.handoff_condition: The client has returned to the Multiplayer server list after `Done` was clicked, the Python terminal has logged that it sent the supplied status payload, and the resulting status description is currently rendered beneath the `MC-306860 Mock Server` entry. Begin observation without joining the server or refreshing the list.
uncertainties: The report specifies that Python must be installed and uses the command form `python _.py`, but it does not specify an operating system or Python installation method. This plan uses Windows-oriented Command Prompt or PowerShell instructions because those are explicitly named in the report.

Some Windows Python installations expose Python 3 through `py` rather than `python`. The report specifically instructs use of `python`, so that command is retained; if it is unavailable, the environment must be corrected or the equivalent launcher selected before continuing.
The report does not specify a server-list display name. `MC-306860 Mock Server` is an arbitrary practical label and does not affect the status payload.

The report does not explicitly discuss firewall prompts or port conflicts. Allowing local Python networking and keeping TCP port 25565 free are practical requirements for executing the supplied script.
No vanilla Minecraft server is used. The supplied Python program only implements enough of the status protocol to answer the Multiplayer server-list query.

source_meta._title: Servers can no longer detect left clicks from players in Spectator mode

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.1, using one authenticated multiplayer-capable account and an internet connection to the third-party dedicated minigame server mc.hypixel.net. The reproduction uses a SkyWars Solo Normal match and Hypixel's post-death spectator flow.
preconditions: Install or create a launcher installation for Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.1; do not use the listed fix version 26.2 Snapshot 7.
Sign in to a Minecraft account that owns Java Edition and is permitted to join online multiplayer servers.
Ensure the client can connect to mc.hypixel.net and that Hypixel currently accepts connections from version 26.1.1.
Use the report-provided public-server reproduction path. No local world, cheats, operator permission, or server console access is involved.

Know the configured controls corresponding to Chat, Attack/Destroy, Use Item/Place Block, movement, jump/fly upward, and sneak/fly downward. The steps name the common defaults: T, left mouse button, right mouse button, W, Space, and Left Shift.
A SkyWars Solo Normal match must be available, and at least one other player must remain alive long enough to be targeted after the test player dies.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that launches Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1.1, and start the game. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition main menu is visible and the selected client version is 26.1.1.

steps.action: From the main menu, select Multiplayer. If the multiplayer safety warning appears, read it and select Proceed to reach the server list.
steps.success_cue: The Java Edition multiplayer server-list screen is visible.

steps.action: Select Direct Connection. If Direct Connection is unavailable, select Add Server instead and use any descriptive server name.
steps.success_cue: A screen containing a Server Address field is open.

steps.action: Enter the report-supplied server address exactly as shown and select Join Server. If using Add Server, enter the address in Server Address, save the entry, select it in the server list, and then select Join Server.
steps.success_cue: The client begins connecting to mc.hypixel.net without an invalid-address error.

steps.action: Wait until the Hypixel lobby has fully loaded. Do not continue while a loading screen is displayed or while movement and chat are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a rendered Hypixel lobby and normal player movement responds to input.

steps.action: Press the Chat control, T by default, to open in-game chat. Type the report-supplied command with the leading slash and press Enter once.
steps.success_cue: Hypixel accepts the command and transfers or queues the player for a SkyWars Solo Normal match rather than displaying an unknown-command error.

steps.action: Wait through matchmaking and the pre-game countdown. Do not leave the starting area before the match begins. After the countdown, wait until the starting restraint or cage is released and player movement is enabled.
steps.success_cue: The SkyWars match is active, nearby islands and the void have rendered, and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Immediately turn toward the nearest edge leading into empty space above the void. Move forward with W and, if needed to clear the edge, press Space to jump. Continue moving until the player has left the island and is falling into the void. Do not engage another player or perform unrelated actions first.
steps.success_cue: The player is visibly falling below the starting island with no blocks beneath them.

steps.action: Allow the void to kill the player. Wait for Hypixel's death transition and post-death spectator state to finish loading; dismiss only any ordinary death overlay or prompt that prevents movement, if one appears.
steps.success_cue: The player is no longer an active SkyWars combatant and can move around using Hypixel's post-death spectator mode.

steps.action: Locate a living SkyWars player. Fly toward that player using the normal movement controls; use Space to rise and the Sneak control, Left Shift by default, to descend if necessary. Approach until the living player's body is within interaction range, then center the crosshair directly on that player.
steps.exact_input: W; Space to rise; Left Shift to descend
steps.success_cue: A living SkyWars player is nearby and centered under the crosshair.

steps.action: With the crosshair still on the nearby living player, press the Use Item/Place Block control, the right mouse button by default, once. This is the report's Hypixel-specific interaction for entering the target player's vanilla-style first-person spectator view.
steps.success_cue: The camera is attached to the living player in first-person spectator view and follows that player's position and view rather than moving independently.

steps.action: While the camera remains attached to the living player in first-person spectator view, press the Attack/Destroy control, the left mouse button by default, exactly once. Do not change targets, exit the view, or click repeatedly before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: One left-click input has just been issued while the client remains attached to the living player's first-person spectator view.

stor.handoff_condition: The Minecraft 26.1.1 client remains in first-person spectator view of a living SkyWars player, and the player has just pressed the left mouse button once. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately, without issuing another click or leaving spectator view.
uncertainties: The report's formal Steps to Reproduce section says N/A. This plan reconstructs the execution path from Comment 2, which the commenter stated was tested with Minecraft 26.1.2.

The structured Affects versions field lists only 26.1.1, so 26.1.1 is retained as the recommended reproduction version. Although the comment mentions testing 26.1.2 and the description also discusses the broader 26.1 release line, those versions were not added to affected_versions.

Hypixel is a live third-party service. Its supported client versions, /play solo_normal command, SkyWars availability, death flow, and right-click spectator interaction may have changed since the report was written. If version 26.1.1 is rejected or the described interaction is no longer available, this report-provided public-server path cannot be completed without an alternative server-side packet monitor or archived server implementation not supplied in the report.

The report calls Hypixel's initial post-death state its version of spectator mode and distinguishes it from the vanilla-style first-person spectator view entered by right-clicking a nearby player. The plan preserves that distinction.

If the targeted player dies, disconnects, or the match ends before step 12, return to the lobby if necessary and restart from the /play solo_normal command rather than triggering the test in a different state.
Control keys may have been rebound. The named keys and mouse buttons are defaults; the executor must use the controls currently bound to the corresponding Minecraft actions.

source_meta._title: Client continues to connect to server after canceling on 'Connecting to server' screen

stor.environment: Use an unmodified Minecraft Java Edition client running exactly Minecraft 1.8 with an authenticated multiplayer account. Provide two distinct, simultaneously available multiplayer servers, designated Server A and Server B, that both accept a Minecraft 1.8 client and the test account. Controlled vanilla-compatible servers are preferred to eliminate unrelated server modifications. Server A must take long enough to connect that the client displays the "Connecting to server..." screen and its Cancel button; if a local Server A connects too quickly, use a more latent endpoint or controlled network delay without modifying Minecraft protocol traffic.
preconditions: Completely exit every Minecraft client process before beginning. The report states that restarting the game clears the lingering connection, so a fresh client process is required for a clean attempt.
Install or configure a Minecraft Launcher installation for the exact affected version Minecraft 1.8. Do not use the fix version 1.20 Pre-release 5.
Have the hostname or IP address and port for two different reachable servers: Server A, whose connection will be canceled, and Server B, which will be joined immediately afterward.

Confirm independently before the reproduction attempt that both servers accept the same authenticated test account when joined normally with Minecraft 1.8. Disconnect normally after each connectivity check, and then restart the client before beginning the actual attempt.
Ensure Server A does not complete world loading so quickly that the "Connecting to server..." screen cannot be canceled. The reproduction must cancel from that screen before Server A's world appears.
Ensure the client is not already connected to a singleplayer world, Realm, or multiplayer server when the procedure begins.

Perform only one cancel-and-switch sequence per fresh client launch. If Server A's world loads before Cancel is activated or any other timing step is missed, fully exit Minecraft and restart from step 1 rather than continuing from a contaminated connection state.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured for exactly Minecraft 1.8, and start the game by clicking Play.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft 1.8 title screen is visible and no world or server is loaded.

steps.action: From the title screen, open the multiplayer server menu by left-clicking Multiplayer once.
steps.success_cue: The Play Multiplayer screen and its server list are visible.

steps.action: If Server A is not already saved, left-click Add Server, enter a recognizable name such as "Server A", enter the Server A hostname or IP address including its port when non-default, and left-click Done. Repeat this process for Server B using its distinct address. Do not configure both entries to resolve to the same server endpoint.
steps.exact_input: Server Name: Server A / Server B; Server Address: addresses supplied by the test environment; buttons: Add Server, Done
steps.success_cue: Two separately named rows, Server A and Server B, are visible in the multiplayer server list and represent different server endpoints.

steps.action: Wait only until the Server A row can be selected. Do not join Server B first, and do not enter another world during this attempt.
steps.success_cue: The multiplayer server list remains interactive and Server A is visible.

steps.action: Left-click Server A once so that its row is highlighted.
steps.success_cue: Server A is the selected server and the Join Server button is available.

steps.action: Start connecting to Server A by left-clicking Join Server once. Do not double-click repeatedly.
steps.success_cue: The full-screen "Connecting to server..." message is visible and the Cancel button is available; Server A's world has not appeared.

steps.action: While the screen still says "Connecting to server...", immediately left-click Cancel exactly once. The click must occur before terrain or an in-game world from Server A appears. If Server A's world appears first, invalidate this attempt, completely exit Minecraft, and restart from step 1.
steps.success_cue: The connecting screen closes and a Minecraft menu is visible without Server A's world ever having been displayed.

steps.action: As soon as control returns, navigate back to the multiplayer server list if necessary. If the title screen is visible, left-click Multiplayer; if the Play Multiplayer screen is already visible, continue without leaving it. Do not idle, refresh the list, or restart the client.
steps.success_cue: The Play Multiplayer screen is visible immediately after canceling the Server A connection.

steps.action: Immediately left-click Server B once to select it. Server B must be different from Server A.
steps.success_cue: Server B is highlighted and the Join Server button is available.

steps.action: Without waiting for the server list to refresh or for additional ping results, left-click Join Server once to begin connecting to Server B.
steps.success_cue: The client leaves the server list and displays the connection or login screen for the second join attempt.

steps.action: Allow the second connection attempt to proceed without pressing Cancel, Escape, or opening another world. Wait until an in-game world view and HUD appear and the client begins accepting normal keyboard and mouse input. Do not disconnect, restart, or evaluate the resulting client state before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: An in-game world view has appeared following the Server B join attempt, with the Minecraft client still running from the same uninterrupted process that canceled Server A.

stor.handoff_condition: The client has just reached an in-game world view after canceling Server A specifically from the "Connecting to server..." screen and immediately initiating a connection to distinct Server B without restarting Minecraft. Hand control to the observation subsystem now so it can inspect the client and both server-side connection states before any disconnect, menu transition, or restart occurs.
uncertainties: The report does not provide reusable addresses or configurations for Server A and Server B. Using two controlled, distinct Minecraft 1.8-compatible servers is therefore a practical implementation choice supported by comments confirming reproduction on vanilla and with arbitrary servers.

The original description names CubeKrowd as the accidentally selected server, but no server address is supplied and the report's later comments confirm that the issue is not restricted to CubeKrowd. This plan does not depend on that historical public server.

The report does not provide an exact maximum delay between canceling Server A and joining Server B. It only establishes that the first connection must be canceled while loading and that the next server should be joined quickly; therefore the plan instructs the executor to act immediately without assigning an unsupported millisecond threshold.

Depending on the exact Minecraft 1.8 menu transition, Cancel may return directly to the multiplayer list or to the title screen. Step 8 handles either state without altering the required connection order.

The first listed affected version, Minecraft 1.8, is used as required. Some comments provide more explicit alternate timing methods for later 1.8.x versions, but those alternatives were not substituted for the primary report's Minecraft 1.8 cancel-and-switch sequence.

A very low-latency local Server A may finish loading before the Cancel action can be performed. The report does not prescribe a particular latency mechanism, so using a naturally latent endpoint or controlled network delay is an execution aid rather than a report-stated requirement.
